atten3.ptxt: Perform A/T learned value initialization 1 minutes or more after connecting the battery terminal.

atten4.ptxt: Learned values are not initialized (cleared) by simply disconnecting the battery negative terminal.

step2.ptxt: Stop the vehicle on a level road surface.
Check that the shift position is in the P range, connect SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3, and turn the ignition ON and the SST power ON.
Perform A/T Learned Value Initialization

step3.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select and execute main menu [Work Support] → work support category [Transmission] → [A/T/CVT Learned Value Initialization] to initialize the A/T learned values.

atten4.ptxt: Initialization takes approximately 1 minutes to complete.

step1.ptxt: A/T Unit Compensation (Manual A/T Code Registration)

atten4.ptxt: When replacing the transaxle assembly (including both ECU-integrated and transaxle-only replacement), perform A/T unit compensation (manual A/T code registration) after replacing the axle.

step2.ptxt: Record the A/T code (5 digits × 12 blocks) printed on the TM label of the supply part.
Complete the transaxle assembly replacement work.
With the IG OFF, connect SST (TaSCAN) to the DLC3 connector.
With the shift lever in the P range, press the IG switch 2 times without depressing the brake pedal to turn the ignition ON.

item.ptxt: The engine will not start.
Do not operate the shift lever or engine switch until the calibration work is complete.

step2.ptxt: Turn the SST (TaSCAN) power ON and select "Diagnosis" → "Diagnosis Item / Work Support" → "Support Category / Transmission" → "A/T Unit Compensation (Manual A/T Code Registration)".
While checking the screen display, press "Next" to proceed to the input screen (step 4/6).
Operate the buttons on the screen to input the A/T code on the TM label in the same positions as on the label, and press "Complete" after input.
Check that the entered A/T code is the same as that on the TM label, and press "Start".
Confirm work completion on the screen.

step1.ptxt: A/T Unit Compensation (A/T Code Read/Save) and A/T Unit Compensation (Automatic A/T Code Registration)

item.ptxt: When replacing only the transmission control computer, perform A/T unit compensation (A/T code read/save) before replacement, and perform A/T unit compensation (automatic A/T code registration) after replacing the computer.
If the A/T code cannot be read due to a malfunction of the transmission control computer, perform A/T unit compensation (A/T code initialization) and then perform driving learning.
Do not perform manual input from the A/T code label affixed to the vehicle transaxle.

step2.ptxt: With the IG OFF, connect SST (TaSCAN) to the DLC3 connector.
With the shift lever in the P range, press the IG switch 2 times without depressing the brake pedal to turn the ignition ON.

item.ptxt: The engine will not start.
Do not operate the shift lever or IG switch until the work is completed.

step2.ptxt: Turn the SST (TaSCAN) power ON and select "Diagnosis" → "Diagnosis Item / Work Support" → "Support Category / Transmission" → "A/T Unit Compensation (Read/Save A/T Code)".
Press "Start" to read the A/T code stored in the transmission control computer.
After reading of the A/T code (5 digits × 12 blocks) is completed, press "Save" to store the A/T code in SST (TaSCAN).

atten4.ptxt: If the A/T code cannot be read, perform driving learning after A/T unit compensation (A/T code initialization).

step2.ptxt: Record the <Save Date/Time> and press "Complete".
Turn the IG OFF and replace the transmission control computer.
After completing the replacement work, set SST (TaSCAN) in the same way as for reading.
From the SST (TaSCAN) screen, select "Diagnosis" → "Diagnosis Item / Work Support" → "Support Category / Transmission" → "A/T Unit Compensation (Automatic A/T Code Registration)".
Press "NEXT", check the save date and time of the A/T code saved in SST (TaSCAN), and press "Start".
Confirm work completion on the screen.

item.ptxt: When the valve body is replaced or either (SL4) of the clutch control solenoids (SL3) is replaced, after completing the replacement perform A/T unit compensation (A/T code initialization) and then perform driving learning.
When replacing clutch control solenoid (SL1) or (SL2), perform driving learning only.

step2.ptxt: Complete the replacement work.
With the IG OFF, connect SST (TaSCAN) to the DLC3 connector.
With the shift lever in the P range, press the IG switch 2 times without depressing the brake pedal to turn the ignition ON.

item.ptxt: The engine will not start.
Do not operate the shift lever or IG switch until the work is completed.

step2.ptxt: Turn the SST (TaSCAN) power ON and select "Diagnosis" → "Diagnosis Item / Work Support" → "Support Category / Transmission" → "A/T Unit Compensation (A/T Code Initialization)".
Start initialization following the screen display and confirm that initialization is completed.

atten2.ptxt: Exercise sufficient caution when performing the driving work.

step2.ptxt: With the IG OFF, connect SST (TaSCAN) to the DLC3 connector.
Depress the brake pedal, turn the ignition ON (START) and start the engine.

Turn the SST (TaSCAN) power ON, select Diagnosis" → "System Diagnosis / Chassis" → "System Name / ECT" → "Diagnosis Function / ECU Data", then select and execute the monitor item "Accelerator Opening".
With the vehicle stopped, check the pedal depression amount that gives an accelerator opening of 15%.
From a vehicle speed of 0km/h, depress the accelerator pedal at an accelerator opening of 15% or less and accelerate to the highest possible vehicle speed while keeping the accelerator constant.
If there is shift shock, repeat until the shift shock disappears.
With the vehicle stopped, check the pedal depression amount that gives an accelerator opening of 25 to 35%.
From a vehicle speed of 0km/h, depress the accelerator to an opening of 25 to 35% and accelerate to the highest possible vehicle speed while keeping the accelerator constant.
If there is shift shock, repeat until the shift shock disappears.

step1.ptxt: CVT Learned Value Initialization, G Sensor 0-point Learning and CVT Hydraulic Pressure Learning

item.ptxt: When the learned values are initialized, both the G sensor 0 point learned value and the CVT hydraulic pressure learned value are cleared.
After initializing the CVT learned values, always perform G sensor 0 point learning first, then perform CVT hydraulic pressure learning.

step2.ptxt: TaSCAN - CVT Learned Value Initialization

step3.ptxt: Turn the IG OFF, move the shift lever to the P position and apply the parking brake.
Turn the IG ON (engine stopped).
Using SST (TaSCAN), following the screen display, select [Utility] from the TOP menu and select [Transmission] in the utility category.
Select [AT/CVT Learned Value Initialization] on the screen to initialize the CVT learned values.

step2.ptxt: TaSCAN - G Sensor 0 Point Learning

item.ptxt: Be sure to place the vehicle on a level surface and perform 0 point learning.
Do not subject the vehicle to vibration while 0 point learning is in progress.
Do not start the engine, to avoid idling vibration.

step3.ptxt: Turn the IG ON (engine stopped) and wait for 2 seconds or more.
Using SST (TaSCAN), following the screen display, select [Utility] from the TOP menu and select [Transmission] in the utility category.
Select [G Sensor 0 Point Learning Start] on the screen to perform G sensor 0 point learning. (*1)

item.ptxt: When [Complete] is displayed on the screen, G sensor 0 point learning is complete.
If [Error] is displayed on the screen and the check engine warning light comes on, there may be a malfunction in the G sensor circuit.

If the vehicle is subjected to vibration during 0 point learning, 0 point learning may be canceled. (If [Error] is displayed on the screen and the check engine warning light does not illuminate) In that case, perform the work in (*1) again.

step2.ptxt: TaSCAN - CVT Hydraulic Pressure Learning

step3.ptxt: Turn the IG OFF and wait for 30 seconds or more.
Turn the IG ON (engine stopped) and wait for 2 seconds or more.
Using SST (TaSCAN), follow the screen instructions to select [Work Support] on the TOP menu, then select [Transmission] in the work support category.
Start the engine and wait for 5 seconds or more.
Select [CVT Hydraulic Pressure Learning Start] on the screen to perform CVT hydraulic pressure learning.

item.ptxt: During CVT hydraulic pressure learning, the engine is in an idle-up state.
CVT hydraulic pressure learning is complete when [Complete] is displayed on the screen.
The CVT hydraulic pressure learned values are not initialized just by disconnecting the battery terminal.

step2.ptxt: Set the steering and front tires to the straight-ahead position.
Disconnect the battery negative terminal for 2 seconds or more.
Connect the battery negative terminal.

atten3.ptxt: Be sure to perform the setting procedures required after disconnecting and reconnecting the battery terminal. (see )

step1.ptxt: Yaw Rate Sensor & G Sensor 0-point Acquisition

atten3.ptxt: Always perform 0 point acquisition on a level surface (gradient within 1%), and do not rock the vehicle or open and close the doors during the procedure. Also, to avoid idling vibration, do not start the engine.

step2.ptxt: Clear Yaw Rate Sensor & G Sensor 0 Point Memory

step3.ptxt: Turn the ignition switch off and connect SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3.
Check that the shift lever is in the P position and the parking brake is applied, then turn the ignition ON.

atten3.ptxt: If 0 point clearing is performed with the shift position other than P, it may not finish normally.

step3.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select and execute [Work Support] → [Support Category / ABS/VSC/Electronically Controlled Brake System] → [Backup Memory Clear].
After completion, turn the ignition OFF within 15 seconds.

atten3.ptxt: After 0 point clearing, if the ignition is left ON for 15 seconds or more with the shift lever in P, only the yaw rate sensor 0 point is stored and the VSC warning goes off. If the vehicle is driven in this condition, G sensor 0 point uncalibrated is stored and a VSC system malfunction is displayed.

step2.ptxt: Acquiring Yaw Rate & G Sensor 0 Point

step3.ptxt: With the shift lever in the P position, turn the ignition switch ON and check that the initial check of the indicators finishes.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select and execute [Diagnosis] → [System Name / ABS/VSC] → [Mode Change] to change to test mode.

After changing to test mode, keep the vehicle stationary for approximately 2 seconds, and check that the "VSC Check" display on the multi-information display in the meter disappears and "VSC TEST MODE" is displayed.

item.ptxt: If test mode is entered with the shift lever in any position other than P, the yaw rate sensor and G sensor 0 point uncalibrated malfunction code is stored.
If the 0 point uncalibrated malfunction code is stored, perform the procedure again from 0 point memory clearing.

atten4.ptxt: After 0 point calibration is completed, the display in the meter changes to the test mode display.

step3.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, select and execute [Diagnosis] → [System Name / ABS/VSC] → [Mode Change] to switch to normal mode.

step1.ptxt: Torque Sensor 0 Point Calibration and Rotation Angle Sensor Output Calibration

item.ptxt: If the steering column assembly or power steering computer assembly has been replaced, or if steering effort differs between left and right, clear the computer correction values and then perform torque sensor 0 point calibration and rotation angle sensor output calibration.
If C1516/16 (torque sensor 0 point calibration incomplete) is stored, torque sensor 0 point calibration cannot be performed, so clear the DTC beforehand.
If C1526/18 (rotation angle sensor output calibration incomplete) is stored, rotation angle sensor output calibration cannot be performed, so clear the DTC beforehand.

step2.ptxt: Pre-calibration Inspection

step3.ptxt: Using SST (TaSCAN), check "IG Power Supply Voltage" in the ECU data monitor.

atten3.ptxt: If the IG voltage is 9V or less, the rotation angle sensor output and torque sensor 0 point cannot be calibrated, so if the value is out of the standard range, replace or charge the battery before performing the calibration.

step2.ptxt: Sensor Correction Value Clearing, Torque Sensor 0 Point Calibration and Rotation Angle Sensor Output Calibration

step3.ptxt: Turn IG OFF.
Connect SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3.
Turn IG ON.

Select "Work Support" → "Electric PS" → "Rotation Angle Sensor Output Calibration" on the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, and following the display, perform sensor correction value initialization → torque sensor 0 point calibration → rotation angle sensor output calibration.

item.ptxt: Keep the steering and front tires in the straight-ahead position.
Never touch the steering wheel during torque sensor 0 point calibration (3 seconds).
Do not turn the steering wheel suddenly during rotation angle sensor output calibration.

atten4.ptxt: Rotation angle sensor output calibration calibrates the outputs of the motor rotation angle sensor and the torque sensor.

atten3.ptxt: If "Initializing System" is displayed on the back guide monitor screen, perform steering sensor neutral point memorization.

step2.ptxt: Steering Sensor Steering Angle Neutral Point Memorization

step3.ptxt: The steering angle neutral point is memorized by turning the steering wheel fully to the left and right on a level road.

atten3.ptxt: Steering sensor neutral point memorization must be performed with the engine running. Therefore, apply the parking brake, depress the brake pedal, move the shift lever to P, and take sufficient care that the vehicle does not move off.

atten4.ptxt: Selecting the "?" button displayed together with "Initializing System" displays the correction method described above.

step1.ptxt: Steering Angle Adjustment and Camera Optical Axis Adjustment

step2.ptxt: Preparation Before Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Set the steering wheel in the straight-ahead position and stop the vehicle.

atten4.ptxt: Before stopping the vehicle, always move the vehicle slightly forward and backward, and check that not only the steering wheel but also the tires are in the straight-ahead position.

step3.ptxt: Adjust the tire pressure to the specified value beforehand.
Place the camera optical axis adjustment target bars in the positions shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: The camera optical axis adjustment target bars are tapes approximately 2.5 cm wide and 2 m long applied to the floor; check the color on the vehicle display and use a color that stands out.

step2.ptxt: Start Diagnosis (see )

atten3.ptxt: The adjustment must be performed with the engine running. Therefore, apply the parking brake, depress the brake pedal, move the shift lever to P, and take sufficient care that the vehicle does not move off.

step3.ptxt: Select "Function Inspection/Adjustment" on the service inspection screen to display the function inspection/adjustment screen.
Select "Camera Optical Axis Adjustment" on the function inspection/adjustment screen to display the steering angle adjustment screen.

step2.ptxt: Steering Angle Adjustment

item.ptxt: If "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in part A, check the DTCs of the HDD navigation system and take action according to the output code. (see )
If "Vehicle Speed Input OK" is displayed in part A, the vehicle speed signal is being input normally, so perform steering angle adjustment.
If the vehicle speed signal has not been input, part A displays "Checking Vehicle Speed" with a red background.
If "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in part A, the screen does not switch even if "Maximum Steering Angle Memory" or "Next" is selected.
If "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in part A, touch "Checking Vehicle Speed" (changes from red to orange) and then perform steering angle adjustment.

step3.ptxt: Check that the steering wheel is in the position for driving the vehicle straight ahead (approximately straight, ±5 degrees or less as a guide), and select "Steering Angle Neutral Point Memory".

After memorizing the steering angle neutral point, turn the steering wheel to the left until it stops, then to the right until it stops, and press "Maximum Steering Angle Memory". (Right may be done first)

At the moment it is pressed, a confirmation beep is output, the steering angle adjustment values (steering angle neutral point and maximum steering angle) are stored, and the screen switches to the camera optical axis adjustment screen.

item.ptxt: The adjustment values are not stored until the beep finishes sounding.
If all input signals are being input normally, the screen automatically switches to the camera optical axis adjustment screen after the maximum steering angle is memorized.
If steering angle adjustment has not been performed or "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in part A, selecting "Next" is not accepted.
Even if no DTC is detected, selecting "Maximum Steering Angle Memory" may not be accepted due to a steering sensor malfunction.
If selecting "Maximum Steering Angle Memory" is not accepted, replace the steering sensor. (see )

step2.ptxt: Camera Optical Axis Adjustment

item.ptxt: If the back door is open, "The back door is open. Close the back door before use." is displayed and camera optical axis adjustment cannot be performed.

If "Back door is open. Close the back door before use." is displayed even though the back door is closed, perform inspection according to Troubleshooting Flowchart ["Back door is open. Close the back door before use." is Displayed Even when Back Door is Closed]. (see )

step3.ptxt: Press switch A or B to rotate C so that it is parallel to the adjustment target bar.
Press switches D, E, F and G to move C left, right, up and down so that the adjustment target bar is in the center of C (center of the red frame).
Select "Next" to display the confirmation screen.

step2.ptxt: Confirmation Screen

step3.ptxt: Check that A (indicating 117 cm from the bumper edge) and the adjustment target bar almost overlap. Also, check that when the steering wheel is in the straight-ahead position, the estimated course line is straight (overlaps the vehicle width extension line).
When "Complete" is selected, the screen changes to the function inspection/adjustment screen and the camera optical axis adjustment value is stored.

item.ptxt: When "Complete" is selected, a confirmation beep is output, the camera optical axis adjustment value is stored, and the display changes to the function inspection/adjustment screen.
The adjustment values are not stored until the beep finishes sounding.

step2.ptxt: Cancel Diagnosis (see )
Steering Angle Adjustment Check

atten4.ptxt: If the steering angle adjustment was performed, check the steering angle adjustment on the back guide monitor screen after canceling diagnosis.

step3.ptxt: On the back guide monitor screen, check that the estimated course line moves in conjunction with the steering wheel until the steering wheel is turned fully to the left or right.

atten4.ptxt: If the estimated course line stops moving before the steering wheel is turned fully to the left or right, the steering angle adjustment value has not been stored correctly, and adjustment must be performed again.

step2.ptxt: Preparation Before Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Set the steering wheel in the straight-ahead position and stop the vehicle.

atten4.ptxt: Before stopping the vehicle, always move the vehicle slightly forward and backward, and check that not only the steering wheel but also the tires are in the straight-ahead position.

step3.ptxt: Adjust the tire pressure to the specified value beforehand.
Place the camera optical axis adjustment target bars in the positions shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: The camera optical axis adjustment target bars are tapes approximately 2.5 cm wide and 2 m long applied to the floor; check the color on the vehicle display and use a color that stands out.

step2.ptxt: Start Diagnosis (see )

atten3.ptxt: The adjustment must be performed with the engine running. Therefore, apply the parking brake, depress the brake pedal, move the shift lever to P, and take sufficient care that the vehicle does not move off.

step3.ptxt: Select "Function Inspection/Adjustment" on the service inspection screen to display the function inspection/adjustment screen.
Select "Camera Optical Axis Adjustment" on the function inspection/adjustment screen to display the steering angle adjustment screen.

step2.ptxt: Steering Angle Adjustment

item.ptxt: If the only adjustment required after vehicle servicing is the camera optical axis adjustment, the steering angle adjustment is not necessary, so select "NEXT".
Do not touch the screen except for "Next".
If "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in part A, check the DTCs of the HDD navigation system and take action according to the output code. (see )
If "Vehicle Speed Input OK" is displayed in area A, the vehicle speed signal is being input normally, so select "NEXT".
If the vehicle speed signal has not been input, part A displays "Checking Vehicle Speed" with a red background.
If "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in area A, the screen does not change even if "NEXT" is selected.
If "Checking Vehicle Speed" (displayed in red) is displayed in part A, touch "Checking Vehicle Speed" (changes from red to orange) and then perform steering angle adjustment.

step2.ptxt: Camera Optical Axis Adjustment

item.ptxt: If the back door is open, "Back door is open. Close the back door before use." is displayed and camera optical axis adjustment cannot be performed.

If "Back door is open. Close the back door before use." is displayed even though the back door is closed, perform inspection according to Troubleshooting Flowchart ["Back door is open. Close the back door before use." is Displayed Even when Back Door is Closed]. (see )

step2.ptxt: Cancel Diagnosis (see )

atten3.ptxt: After initializing the headlight leveling computer assembly, perform headlight aim adjustment.

step2.ptxt: Check Vehicle Condition (*1)

step3.ptxt: Put the vehicle in the following condition.

item.ptxt: Reduce the remaining fuel to approximately 10 liters or less.
Unload any removable luggage from the vehicle. (Spare tire and on-board tools remain loaded)
No occupants.
Headlights off.
Vehicle stopped with no change in vehicle height. (Vehicle stable on a level surface)

atten4.ptxt: If the above is not performed, initialization cannot be performed normally.

step2.ptxt: Check Warning Display

step3.ptxt: 3 seconds after turning the ignition OFF → ON, check the warning display of the headlight leveling warning light in the combination meter.

entry.ptxt: Initialization malfunction or headlight leveling computer assembly replaced (new)
Height control sensor replacement/removal, suspension replacement, etc.

atten4.ptxt: If not within the standard, inspect the headlight leveling computer assembly, wire harness and connectors.

step2.ptxt: Initialization Operation

step3.ptxt: Using SST, connect terminals 8 (LVL) ←→ 4 (CG) of connector DLC3.
Within 20 seconds after connecting the initialization terminals, operate the light control switch OFF → HEAD 3 times or more. (*2)

atten3.ptxt: Operate the switch at 1 second intervals.

step3.ptxt: Check the warning display.

entry.ptxt: Blinks 2Hz 2 times → blinks 2Hz 3 times, then goes off (initialization completed normally)
Height control sensor replacement/removal, suspension replacement, etc.
No blinking → blinks 2Hz 3 times, then goes off (initialization completed normally)

atten4.ptxt: If the operation (*2) does not finish normally even after repeating it 20 times or more, start again from step (*1).

item.ptxt: When replacing the navigation receiver assembly on a vehicle not subscribed to the G-BOOK service, perform the vehicle linking setting.

When replacing the navigation receiver assembly on a vehicle subscribed to the G-BOOK service, perform the vehicle linking setting, then perform the G-BOOK use resumption operation and HELPNET service start operation.
If the navigation receiver assembly is replaced while a purchased G-SOUND unlimited license exists, perform G-SOUND license recovery.

step2.ptxt: Contact G-BOOK Support Center

step3.ptxt: Contact the G-BOOK Support Center to inform them that the vehicle association setting will be performed.

atten4.ptxt: After contacting the G-BOOK Support Center, a "Vehicle Association Setting Request Form" will be sent by FAX from the Support Center. Therefore, have the FAX number noted beforehand.

step2.ptxt: Check ID Before Replacement (When Diagnosis Can Be Started)

item.ptxt: If diagnosis can be started, check the ID before performing the replacement.
When replacing the navigation receiver assembly, check the G-BOOK terminal ID.

step3.ptxt: Start diagnosis and display the diagnosis inspection menu screen. (see )
Select "G Terminal Information" on the diagnosis check menu screen to display the G terminal information screen.

item.ptxt: When a power window regulator motor assembly (any seat) is replaced with a new one, DTC B2313 is output. After resetting the power window (initializing the pulse sensor), clear the DTC.

If the door window regulator of any seat has been replaced, or the power window regulator motor assembly (any seat) has been removed from the door window regulator, the power window regulator motor assembly (applicable seat) must be returned to the uninitialized state (current memory of the pulse sensor in the motor cleared) and then the glass position must be reset (pulse sensor initialized). If the reset is not performed, the jam protection function may operate at times other than its operating conditions.

If AUTO UP is operated for a seat after replacing its glass, glass run, etc., the jam protection function may operate. In that case, holding AUTO UP until the door glass of the applicable seat is in the fully closed position will make that seat operate normally.
If the reset cannot be completed normally, LIN communication may be malfunctioning, so inspect the Body Multiplex Communication System [LIN] (see ).

step2.ptxt: Connect the battery and turn the ignition ON; at this time, the indicators of the power window regulator switch assembly, rear power window regulator switch assembly and power window regulator master switch assembly for the location where the power window regulator motor assembly was replaced or removed/installed blink, and the system enters the reset standby state.

item.ptxt: If the indicator does not blink and the jam protection function operates outside its operating conditions, perform the following work to return the power window regulator motor assembly (applicable seat) to the uninitialized state (current memory of the pulse sensor in the motor cleared), then proceed.
While the power window of the applicable seat is operating, disconnect the connector of the power window regulator motor assembly (applicable seat) or disconnect the battery negative terminal.

step2.ptxt: After the glass is fully closed, operate the applicable seat switch on the power window regulator master switch assembly or the applicable seat power window switch for 1 seconds or more (hold AUTO UP); the power window (applicable seat) position is reset, the indicators of the power window regulator master switch assembly and the power window switch (applicable seat) change from blinking to illuminated, and the reset is complete.

atten4.ptxt: If the switch indicator does not change from blinking to illuminated even after performing the above operation, lower the glass 50 mm or more and perform the above operation again.

step1.ptxt: Distance Control Computer Assembly Initial Setting

step2.ptxt: Turn IG ON.
Turn the cruise control main switch ON.
With the brake pedal depressed, push the cruise control main switch in the RES/ACC direction 3 times within 3 seconds and check that the buzzer sounds.

item.ptxt: Perform the measurement on a level floor.

Check that there are no metal objects in the surrounding area or on the floor surface. (The area approximately 10m ahead and approximately 14m wide is a prohibited area for objects. It is preferable that there are no large metal objects around it either.)

step2.ptxt: Pre-adjustment Work

step3.ptxt: Unload all luggage from the vehicle.
Leave only the standard tools and spare tire in the trunk.
Adjust the tire pressure to the specified value.
Reduce the remaining fuel to less than 15L.

step2.ptxt: Vertical Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Remove dust and oil from the level shelf of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly.
Place the dedicated level in the center of the level shelf of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly.
Turn the vertical adjustment bolt A of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly to adjust so that the bubble is on the red line of the level.

atten4.ptxt: Adjustment range within red frame of level ±0.2°

item.ptxt: Upward: turn bolt A to the minus side
Downward: turn bolt A to the plus side

entry.ptxt: 1 turn of the screwdriver moves it approximately 0.12°

step2.ptxt: Reflector (SST) Height Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Set the reflector (SST) at a height of 70cm from the ground.

step2.ptxt: Reflector (SST) Installation

step3.ptxt: Hang a pointed weight from the center (emblem center) of the front and rear bumpers of the vehicle, and accurately mark the center positions on the floor surface.
Make a mark 5m ahead of the vehicle on the line connecting the 2 front and rear points.

atten4.ptxt: Fix one end of a string to the rear mark, and from 5m ahead of the vehicle, move the other end of the string left and right to align it with the front mark and establish a straight line.

step3.ptxt: Install the reflector (SST) at a position offset 12mm to the left of the vehicle from the marked position.

step2.ptxt: Beam Axis Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Connect SST (TaSCAN) to the vehicle.
Turn IG ON.
Turn the cruise control main switch ON.
On the screen, select "Work Support" → "Radar Cruise" → "Millimeter Wave Radar Beam Axis Adjustment" in that order.
Follow the screen instructions and press the "Start" button.

atten3.ptxt: Check that the beam axis distance is approximately 5m.

step2.ptxt: Horizontal Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Read the current angle deviation.
Based on the beam axis deviation measurement result, use a screwdriver to turn the horizontal adjustment bolt B of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly to adjust it.

item.ptxt: Rightward: turn bolt B to the plus side
Leftward: turn bolt B to the minus side

entry.ptxt: 1 turn of the screwdriver moves it approximately 0.05°

atten3.ptxt: If it is difficult to reach 0°, an object other than the reflector (SST) may be being targeted, so check again for any highly reflective objects in the surrounding area.

step3.ptxt: To reset the driving learned values, cover the right half of the sensor with aluminum foil etc. (a metal object that blocks radio waves). (For approximately 10 seconds)

atten3.ptxt: At this time, leave the reflector (SST) installed, and make sure there is nothing between the right half of the sensor and the reflector.

atten4.ptxt: When reset, the buzzer sounds for 10 seconds and the screen displays "Beam Axis Deviation 6.3°" and "Beam Axis Distance 6.3m".

step3.ptxt: Press the "Complete" button to end the beam axis adjustment mode.
Disconnect SST (TaSCAN) from the vehicle.

step2.ptxt: Recheck Vertical Adjustment

step3.ptxt: Place the dedicated level in the center of the level shelf of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly.
Using a screwdriver, turn the vertical adjustment bolt A of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly to readjust so that the bubble is on the red line of the level.

atten4.ptxt: Adjustment range within red frame of level ±0.2°

item.ptxt: Upward: turn bolt A to the minus side
Downward: turn bolt A to the plus side

entry.ptxt: 1 turn of the screwdriver moves it approximately 0.12°
